subject: Order form: consent & triage for model training and product use
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@orbitech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@orbitech.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Order form questions — training consent & output use

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. We have a couple of outstanding questions from legal about IP and product use before we sign:

1) Training / model use: the draft MSA references a broad feedback license. Orbitech needs to confirm whether Redwood will be allowed to use customer data or outputs to further train models, even if only for quality improvements. Can you confirm the exact scope you expect?

2) Output ownership: our product team needs explicit confirmation that Orbitech retains title to customer-generated outputs, and that Redwood will not assert ownership or downstream commercialize those outputs.

3) Telemetry / telemetry retention: we need clear retention limits for logs and any telemetry tied to customer inputs.

I'm attaching the OrderForm_Orbitech_signed_draft.pdf with our suggested non-substantive edits. If we can get a short summary of Redwood's stance on the three points above, legal can decide whether the redlines are acceptable or if we need a call.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Legal
Orbitech

Attachment(s): OrderForm_Orbitech_signed_draft.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@orbitech.com>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@orbitech.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Order form questions — training consent & output use

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear note and the PDF. Looping in Grace (Product) and Ben (Sales/legal liaison) so they're sighted. Quick summary of Redwood's position and a proposed path forward:

- Training / model use: Redwood's standard stance for Order Forms is: no training on customer data or outputs by default. We request a limited, non-exclusive feedback license that allows us to use anonymized telemetry/aggregates for quality improvements, but only if customer explicitly opts in on the Order Form.

- Output ownership: we accept customer ownership of outputs. We'll add explicit language to the Order Form stating Orbitech retains title to outputs and that Redwood will not assert ownership or commercialize Orbitech outputs.

- Telemetry retention: standard is 90 days for input-level logs in hosted mode unless a longer retention is contracted (we can add a clause for custom retention schedules in Dedicated or Private deployments).

Attached is a working redline to the MSA that includes: an opt-in checkbox for "Training & model retrain consent", explicit output ownership language, and a 90-day telemetry baseline. Please review. If those points are acceptable to Orbitech, we can finalize and move to DocuSign. If any of these are blockers, happy to jump on a short call.

Proposed next steps (short):
- Elena: confirm Opt-in checkbox + telemetry baseline OK (yes/no)
- Sanjay: confirm procurement timeline and any compliance evidence required (SOC2 / KMS)
- Grace: if we add specialized retention or private deployment language, we will produce a scope note and cost delta.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Dir, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): Orbitech_MSA_redline_v2.docx

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@orbitech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay@orbitech.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:20:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Order form questions — training consent & output use

Thanks Marissa — brief product note from my side.

- The opt-in for training should be explicit and scoped to model-improvement only; it must exclude any downstream productization rights. I recommend the opt-in checkbox language read: "Customer consents to Redwood's use of anonymized, aggregated telemetry and feedback solely for model quality improvements; such use does not grant Redwood rights to customer outputs or proprietary data."

- For telemetry retention, 90 days is a good baseline. If Orbitech expects longer retention for debug/audit, we'll need to qualify whether that telemetry remains in customer-only logs (Dedicated/Private) or is included in the anonymized aggregate set for product improvement.

- Implementation note: we'll add a config switch in the Console that the account admin can toggle for the opt-in; if disabled, we will not include any Orbitech data in training/aggregates. This will simplify ops and provide a clear audit trail.

Happy to provide the short paragraph to insert into the Order Form.

Grace
VP, Product — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@orbitech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay@orbitech.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:55:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Order form questions — training consent & output use

Elena / Sanjay — quick note from the contract side after reviewing the redline:

- Section to change: MSA §4.3 (Feedback; Model Improvements). Proposed insertion: "Customer retains all right, title, and interest in Customer Outputs. Customer may, at its sole election and via explicit opt-in on the applicable Order Form, grant Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use anonymized, aggregated telemetry and feedback for model quality improvements only; such license does not permit Redwood to train customer-specific models or commercialize Customer Outputs."

- We will also add a telemetry schedule table to the Order Form showing default retention (90 days) and optional tiers (180 / 365 days) with pricing deltas for hosted mode.

- Compliance evidence: we can push SOC 2 Type II report, SOC-validated data flow diagrams, and a summary of KMS controls during procurement. If Orbitech needs an HSM integration, that'll be scoped separately.

If that language looks good I can have Legal pre-approve it and we can circulate the doc for signature next week.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@orbitech.com>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay@orbitech.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:43:00 -0500
Subject: Final: Order Form & MSA redlines — next steps

Elena / Sanjay — thanks for the quick review and the helpful notes. Per Ben and Grace above, here's the agreed path and attachments:

- Redwood will accept Orbitech ownership of Customer Outputs. We will add explicit language to the MSA and Order Form as drafted (see attached Orbitech_MSA_redline_v2.docx).
- Training: default = no training. Customer opt-in available on the Order Form ("Training & model retrain consent"). If Orbitech checks that box, Redwood may use anonymized, aggregated telemetry for model quality improvements only; Redwood will not use data to commercialize customer outputs or produce customer-specific models.
- Telemetry retention: default 90 days for hosted accounts; Dedicated/Private options available with custom retention schedules (we'll provide a pricing table).
- Compliance: attaching links to SOC2 report and a procurement pack. If you confirm, we'll upload the final to DocuSign and route to your signature.

Action items:
- Elena: confirm "opt-in" language and 90-day baseline are acceptable (reply yes/no).
- Sanjay: confirm procurement timeline and share any additional compliance requests.
- Marissa/Ben/Grace: we'll prep the final DocuSign envelope and HubSpot deal update once we have Orbitech confirmation.

Thanks — aiming to close this by EOD Monday if possible.

Marissa Cole
Dir, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
